Azure SQL and SQL Server

Source: vignettes/azure-sql.Rmd
azure-sql.Rmd

Azure SQL is Microsoft’s hosted SQL database; SQL Server can also run on your own infrastructure. Let people sign in with their Microsoft account and query Azure SQL from your Shiny app. Their database permissions determine which data they can see.

oauth_db_azure_sql() provides a connection for ordinary DBI or dbplyr queries. The app below starts by listing the tables the user can access.

Try the guided demo

Run shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_cloud_demo("azure-sql") in your R console. The guide asks for server, database, Entra tenant_id and client_id, then your registration type. It explains the database user/group setup, firewall access and delegated SQL permission separately from app consent. You can save a draft while an administrator arranges access.

Install odbc, processx, askpass and Microsoft ODBC Driver 18 first. The editable local app waits for Run example query before connecting. For scripts, supply the settings above; optional driver and database_port configure the native connection. The Shiny callback’s port is separate. A confidential registration uses OAUTHDB_AZURE_SQL_CLIENT_SECRET or masked input. See Guided cloud demos.

If you need an account and database, check the Azure SQL free offer. Availability and allowances depend on your subscription; stopping the local app does not stop Azure billing or pause its database.

Set up access

In R, run install.packages("odbc"), then install Microsoft ODBC Driver 18 for your operating system. Your database administrator must enable Microsoft Entra authentication and give users or their groups access to the database.

Create a Microsoft Entra Web app registration with permission to access SQL on a user’s behalf. Register http://localhost:8100 as its redirect URI, then save these values in a local .Renviron file and restart R:

OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID=your-tenant-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret

Follow Microsoft app registration to find the IDs and secret. Add the Azure SQL Database delegated user_impersonation permission and obtain consent as your tenant requires.

Value in the app Where to find it
server Azure portal: SQL database overview, Server name
database The database’s name in Azure, not the logical server name
Tenant ID and client ID Entra app registration overview
Client secret Registration’s Certificates & secrets, secret Value

In Azure, allow the app server’s IP or private network to reach SQL. Creating an app registration doesn’t open the database firewall.

A complete app

Save this as app.R, replacing the server and database:

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_microsoft_client(
  services = "sql",
  tenant_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID"),
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(fluidPage(
  actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
  actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
  tableOutput("rows")
), id = "auth", client = client)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_azure_sql(
    auth$connection,
    server = "example.database.windows.net",
    database = "Reporting"
  )

  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT TOP (20) name FROM sys.tables")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(port = 8100), uiPattern = ".*")

Run shiny::runApp(port = 8100) from the app directory and open http://localhost:8100. Sign in to run the query; signing out clears the output.

Give users database access

An administrator first sets an Entra administrator on the Azure SQL logical server. Connect to the target database with that administrator and create an external user or group, then grant the intended access. For example:

CREATE USER [reporting-readers] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER;
GRANT SELECT ON OBJECT::dbo.Orders TO [reporting-readers];

Use an existing Entra group name and your actual table. This establishes database permissions for its members; OAuth registration alone doesn’t. Microsoft’s Entra configuration guide covers administrator setup and external users.

Query with dbplyr

In the app, con is a function. Calling con() inside renderTable() gets the signed-in user’s DBI connection.

To read an Orders table with dbplyr, install dbplyr and dplyr, then replace the output expression with:

output$rows <- renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  dplyr::tbl(connection, "Orders") |>
    dplyr::filter(amount > 100) |>
    dplyr::collect()
})

For SQL queries that include values entered by a user, use DBI parameter binding.

Other SQL Server deployments

Use the same oauth_db_azure_sql() helper for SQL Managed Instance or Synapse SQL, with that deployment’s server and database. For SQL Server configured to accept Entra tokens, use oauth_db_sql_server() with the same arguments and client.

See ?oauth_db_azure_sql for driver settings such as driver, port, and timeout. Authentication and sessions covers custom permissions and existing logins.
